subject: ILCE-6400 Taiwan 2.00 target feature boundaries

observations.source: ILCE-6400 Taiwan 2.00 FirmwareData.dat and extracted target filesystem fingerprints in this report
observations.claim: The official updater contains a bounded CXD90045 target for model 0x81030011, and the historical reader successfully unpacked 1,079 target filesystem entries offline.

observations.source: lib/viewUnified2.so, lib/viewUnified7.so, master_camera.uxc, and viewStlrec.uxc fingerprints in this report
observations.claim: ViewStlrec registers the new orientation-roll service as consumer bit 2, attaches layout-mode updates, and five vertical-named shooting layout classes are accepted by the layout factory and referenced by target UXC resources.

observations.source: lib/viewUnified2.so fingerprint and recorded call offsets in this report
observations.claim: The target has low-level resource touch routing and a touch-capable selection widget, but no direct resource touch start or stop call was found in the ViewSettingMenu region.

observations.source: lib/viewUnified2.so ViewSettingMenu event switch at 0x22355e and schema-v2 offline direct-call trace
observations.claim: The recovered settings-menu event graph reaches a touch detect-mode status read through 0x222f68 and 0x43156c, plus display-transition touch-pad area reconfiguration through 0x21c644 and 0x41ae08; neither path consumes coordinates or dispatches a menu selection.

observations.source: lib/libObj.so SampleView vtable/RTTI, resource setup at 0x6666a4, and ObjDisplay backup reads at 0xdc30b6 and 0xdc597a
observations.claim: Backup 0x01050002 conditionally skips resource touch setup inside SampleView, while the separately identified BKID_DISPLAY_TP_DEVICE key is 0x002a000a; no production-menu link or code link between these two keys has been established.

observations.source: eleven parsed Sony backup images, lib/CautionConfig.so graph selector at 0x7db958, and compiled node tables
observations.claim: Every regional backup image stores read-only selector 0x01070316 as 0x43, which maps to the 91-node TypeEmnt Creative Style graph; the 98-node Default graph and 19-node Type07 graph are compiled but not selected.

observations.source: eleven parsed revision-4 Sony backup images in 0110_backup/SYSASTRA-DSLR/DX2
observations.claim: All regional images agree that BKID_DISPLAY_TP_DEVICE and the SampleView touch gate default to 1, while the read-only resource-touch configuration defaults to 0x28.
Sony documents three adjustable Creative Style parameters on the ILCE-6400: contrast, saturation, and sharpness.
Sony documents eight adjustable Creative Look parameters on the ILCE-6700, including highlights, shadows, fade, sharpness range, and clarity beyond the three target axes.

inferences.source: ViewStlrec vtable/RTTI ownership, orientation registration, target UXC records, and the unguarded target layout factory
inferences.claim: The vertical-named layouts are target-resident shooting components rather than strings alone, but their names do not establish device-rotation semantics and no orientation-to-layout selector was found.

inferences.source: Shipped backup defaults, TypeEmnt graph shape, and official adjustment-axis documentation
inferences.claim: The α6400's shipped 0x43 selector and 91-node TypeEmnt graph account for 13 fixed styles plus six groups of 13 selectable box bases; those six Style Boxes remain the safest target-native storage for approximate Creative Look recipes.

inferences.source: ViewSettingMenu direct-call trace, SampleView ownership, and low-level target touch APIs
inferences.claim: The production settings menu is aware of touch status and display-transition touch-pad state, but full menu touch still requires an unlocated coordinate consumer, selection dispatcher, and production resource binding; the writable SampleView gate is not evidence of a hidden global enable switch.

unresolved.source: ViewStlrec event dispatch, AF-orientation branch, and layout-mode handlers
unresolved.claim: ViewStlrec uses camera orientation for AF-coordinate handling, but no exact orientation event that selects the vertical-named layouts or any matching touch-coordinate transform has been proven.

unresolved.source: ViewSettingMenu UXC and widget event graph
unresolved.claim: No coordinate consumer, menu-selection dispatcher, or production resource hook was recovered from the bounded ViewSettingMenu direct-call graph; indirect and data-driven dispatch remain untested, and the blocking resource or product predicate has not been isolated.

unresolved.source: ILCE-6400 target rendering pipeline versus ILCE-6700 Creative Look behavior
unresolved.claim: No native implementations of the five additional Creative Look adjustment axes or exact donor look algorithms have been located in the target.

unresolved.source: Read-only Creative Style selector 0x01070316 and compiled alternate graphs
unresolved.claim: The runtime consequences of forcing an alternate compiled graph are unknown, the normal backup API marks the selector read-only, and no mutation has been attempted.
An authenticated package reconstruction and safe install path remain absent, so none of the target feature hypotheses can be installed.

conclusion: The stock ILCE-6400 image contains vertical-named shooting layouts, orientation-aware AF handling, low-level touch machinery, and a richer Creative Style graph than its interface exposes. Sony backup images prove the selected read-only 0x43 TypeEmnt graph, while vtable evidence limits the writable touch gate to SampleView rather than the production menu. The ViewSettingMenu event graph reaches touch-status reads and display-transition touch-pad reconfiguration, but no recovered direct path consumes coordinates or dispatches a menu selection. ViewStlrec subscribes to the new roll service and separately attaches layout-mode updates, but no call or UXC predicate links roll state to the vertical-named layouts; their names alone do not prove device-rotation semantics. The evidence does not establish the modern rotating menu, full menu touch, native Creative Look, a safe selector mutation, a bypass, or an installable package.
